items.title: Nvidia shares fall in premarket trading as Jensen Huang’s return sparks US political backlash – business live
items.desc: Republicans and Democrats object over Trump’s role in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy Republican senators criticize Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang Congress to grill Jensen Huang over ties with China and Trump’s intervention Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, despite concerns over his conduct and the supply of AI chips to China, may show that AI – and Huang himself – are ‘too big to fail’. That phrase was on everyone’s lips almost 20 years ago when the Global Financial Crisis struck, and several major banks were bailed out. Given Nvidia’s pivotal role in the AI capex rollout, the implications of Huang’s reinstatement could be profound. Borrowing from the GFC, are some technology CEOs now so systemically important to the future of AI and US leadership in the latest technology revolution that they cannot be fired? Questions aro

items.title: Timms says Pip review being published today will ‘rehumanise’ benefit – UK politics live
items.desc: Some recommendations expected to clash with those of Milburn’s recent report into Neets UK disability benefit cuts ‘risk worsening youth destitution’ Q: Will the leave side being split increase the chances of people to rejoin? Farage did not accept the leave side was split. He suggested the Tories were not really party of the leave side. He said: I do not trust the Conservative party on this issue. I trusted them back in 2019. I felt it was the right thing to do. I will never trust them again. And there’s no evidence to suggest that many of millions of others should do so. Yes, I am furious, but I can see where we’ve diverged, we’re doing well. But for most voters out there, reducing the population explosion through mass migration was the key determining factor. They’re disappointed in it, but they’re never going to vote to rejoin, believe you me. Continue reading...

items.title: Burnham says it would be ‘unthinkable’ for the UK to rejoin the EU without a referendum – as it happened
items.desc: The prime minister’s remarks were the clearest commitment yet to not joining the EU without another vote In her speech, Louise Haigh announced that Juergen Maier, chair of Great British Energy, has been appointed as the government’s northern economy and reindustrialisation commissioner. She said: Giving business the confidence to invest here, and create good jobs in our industrial heartlands. Creating good quality jobs in all parts of the country. The role of the private sector is essential to fulfilling that. That is why I am delighted to announce today a new northern economy and reindustrialisation commissioner. items.title: ‘Scapegoating’: green groups condemn plan to axe Environment Agency and Natural England
items.desc: Ministers proposing to abolish the quangos in attempt to give politicians more control over what gets built and where Scientists have accused the government of scapegoating nature for proposing to scrap the only environmental regulator with a legal duty to protect the natural world. Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, said on Monday that the independent regulator Natural England and the Environment Agency were being reviewed as part of a wider shake-up of quangos, or arm’s length bodies. Ministers are considering abolishing the two biggest environmental regulators in an attempt to give politicians greater control over what gets built and where. Continue reading...

items.title: Talk of scrapping Natural England smacks of a government not joining the dots
items.desc: Environmentalists say abolishing independent body will make it easier for landowners and developers ‘to trash nature’ Not just any quango, Natural England is the only public body that exists to legally protect the jewels in the crown of English nature – places increasingly under threat in a country that is overseeing an ongoing and devastating decline in its natural world. Ecologists who work for Natural England are independent, and have the legal duty to scrutinise political decisions and ensure that short-term gallops for growth are not allowed to bulldoze forever rare and declining habitats.
